import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Dataset provided as a string
csv_data = """Person ID,Gender,Age,Occupation,Sleep Duration,Quality of Sleep,Physical Activity Level,Stress Level,BMI Category,Blood Pressure,Heart Rate,Daily Steps,Sleep Disorder
1,Male,27,Software Engineer,6.1,6,42,6,Overweight,126/83,77,4200,
2,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
3,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
4,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
5,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Visualize Sleep Duration by BMI Category, colored by Stress Level.
# A swarmplot is chosen to display individual data points, which is effective
# for showing distribution within categories, especially with a small dataset.
sns.swarmplot(
    data=df,
    x='BMI Category',
    y='Sleep Duration',
    hue='Stress Level', # Differentiate points by Stress Level using color
    size=8,             # Increase point size for better visibility
    palette='viridis',  # Use a perceptually uniform colormap
    edgecolor='gray',   # Add a subtle edge to points
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Add informative title and labels
plt.title('Sleep Duration by BMI Category and Stress Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('BMI Category', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)

# Improve the legend placement and title
plt.legend(title='Stress Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/legend from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png')
